question: Denmark wants to protect boulder reefs in its waters from beam trawling; the areas concerned include the Natura 2000 sites Gule Rev and Jyske Rev. Beam trawling is one of the most destructive forms of fishing. Article 6(2) of the Habitats Directive requires Member States to take the necessary steps in relation to activities that could be ‘significant’ as regards achieving favourable conservation status. 1.

Does the Commission consider that beam trawling can have a destructive impact on the boulder reefs that are the basis for designation as Natura 2000 sites and that Member States are therefore obliged to stop that form of fishing in areas whose site designation is based on boulder reefs?

Can the Commission say whether Belgian beam trawlers use chain mats at Natura 2000 sites and whether the Netherlands or Belgium gives its fishing fleet fuel subsidy support or other support similar to fuel subsidies? If so, what support and how much support is involved?

Does the Commission know when Denmark began work on protecting its Natura 2000 sites from beam trawling, and does it consider that fishing with chain mats at Natura 2000 sites designated on the basis of natural habitats such as boulder reefs calls for it to introduce urgent measures pursuant to Article 11(4) of Regulation (EU) No 1380/2013?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.5.2024) 1. The use of mobile bottom contacting gears such as beam trawls is known to adversely affect boulder reefs. Member States must implement the necessary conservation measures for Natura 2000 sites to avoid deterioration of habitats for which the sites have been designated. This includes regulating fishing activities in accordance with the common fisheries policy1. 2.

Member States have no obligation to report on the use of chain mats, but gears must comply with the technical characteristics stipulated in the Technical Measures Regulation2. Fuel taxation rebates are covered by the General Block Exemption Regulation (GBER)3 which is not sector-specific. Total measures under the GBER applied by Belgium and the Netherlands from 2016 to 2022 were EUR 59.95 million and EUR 37.

3 million respectively, but the information collected does not allow to determine whether and how much fishing fleets may benefit from them. According to Article 14 of the Energy Taxation Directive4, Member States must exempt from taxation energy products supplied for use as fuel for the purposes of navigation within Community waters (including fishing). 3.

Denmark and other concerned Member States submitted the first joint recommendation5 for relevant measures in 20156. A joint recommendation to protect reefs in five Natura 2000 sites in the Danish part of the North Sea and Skagerrak, including Gule Rev and Jyske Rev, has been developed by Denmark together with other Member States concerned7.
In this context, the conditions for the adoption of the urgent measures provided for in Article 11(4) of Regulation (EU) No 1380/2013 are not met.
1 SWD (2018) 288 final. Commission Staff Working Document on the establishment of conservation measures
under the Common Fisheries Policy for Natura 2000 sites and for Marine Strategy Framework Directive purposes.

2 Regulation (EU) 2019/1241 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 June 2019 on the conservation of fisheries resources and the protection of marine ecosystems through technical measures, amending Council Regulations (EC) No 1967/2006, (EC) No 1224/2009 and Regulations (EU) No 1380/2013, (EU) 2016/1139, (EU) 2018/973, (EU) 2019/472 and (EU) 2019/1022 of the European Parliament and of the Council, and repealing Council Regulations (EC) No 894/97, (EC) No 850/98, (EC) No 2549/2000, (EC) No 254/2002, (EC) No 812/2004 and (EC) No 2187/2005.

3 https://competition-policy.ec.europa.eu/state-aid/legislation/regulations_en 4 Council Directive 2003/96/EC of 27 October 2003 restructuring the Community framework for the taxation of energy products and electricity, OJ L 283, 31.10.2003, p. 51–70.

5 Pursuant to Article 11 of Regulation (EU) No 1380/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 December 2013 on the Common Fisheries Policy, amending Council Regulations (EC) No 1954/2003 and (EC) No 1224/2009 and repealing Council Regulations (EC) No 2371/2002 and (EC) No 639/2004 and Council Decision 2004/585/EC, OJ L 354, 28.12.2013, p. 22–61.

The measures comprise the prohibition of fishing activities with mobile bottom contacting gear in reef zones and the prohibition of all fishing activities in bubbling reef zones.
